text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.87% today, bouncing modestly after a steep 8.24% two-week decline. The small gain came as oil prices stabilized—US crude held at $99.64 per barrel after dipping earlier in the week on optimism about Iran tensions easing. The company's earnings report on November 5th and analyst attention haven't offset the broader pullback in energy stocks over the past two weeks.

The real headwind has been geopolitical uncertainty around Iran. Brent crude briefly fell below $90 a barrel earlier this week on hopes for de-escalation, which would increase global oil supply and put downward pressure on the prices that oil producers like ConocoPhillips depend on. Even as today's bounce suggests some steadying, the risk premium has come out of crude—and with it, out of the stock.
